newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore politician found guilty of libel.
newsitem.headline: Singapore politician found guilty of libel.

text.p: Singapore's High Court on Monday found an opposition politician guilty of libeling Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and other ruling party members during an election campaign in December.

Justice Goh Joon Seng said Tang Liang Hong, who fled abroad shortly after the polls, had presented no defence, and the judge therefore found in favour of the ruling People's Action Party (PAP) litigants.
Justice Goh, who is not related to the prime minister, said he would set a date later for a hearing to determine the damages and costs Tang would have to pay.
The High Court earlier ordered Tang to declare assets worth Singapore $11.2 million (US$7.9 million) to cover damages if he was found guilty.
Tang stood unsuccessfully for the Worker's Party in January 2 general elections in which the PAP won 81 of parliament's 83 seats.
Tang fled the city-state shortly after the poll saying he feared for his life. His whereabouts are unknown.

The PAP, led by the prime minister, accused Tang of being a "Chinese chauvinist" who threatened racial harmony in Singapore, where more than 70 percent of the population is ethnic Chinese and contains significant numbers of Malays and Indians.
Tang called the PAP leaders liars and was hit by a deluge of 12 libel suits.
Tang, a lawyer, alleged the suits were intended to destroy him financially and politically. The PAP leaders denied the charge, saying they had to defend their integrity after being called liars.
His case collapsed when he failed to turn up on Monday and his laywer, Worker's Party leader Joshua Jeyaretnam, tried unsuccessfuly to withdraw from the case.

"I can only say he is fearful of his liberty," Jeyaretnam told the court when the judge asked why Tang had not shown up. Jeyaretnam said he had received no instructions from Tang and so could not argue for him.
Lawyers for Goh Chok Tong, Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew and the other PAP ligitants accused Tang of delaying tactics and called on Justice Goh to find him guilty in absentia.
Goh did so in a rare evening session and Tang suffered for the second time in the day.
At an earlier hearing, Tang's petitions over a separate libel case involving Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew were dismissed and Tang was ordered to pay costs.

Justice Lai Kew Chai ruled that Tang had failed to comply with several orders to appear to explain allegations he had made. The case resulted from comments he made in a magazine interview about discounts on properties bought by Lee and his son, Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong.
Tang had asked Justice Lai to withdraw from the case, alleging "perceived bias" in the outcome because Lai had worked for 13 years for the legal firm that Lee Kuan Yew founded.

Tang also said Lai was "a close friend of the Lee family" and had bought a flat at a discount in the same new development as the two Lees in a sale which caused much debate in Singapore, including in parliament.
"My client is saying that you (Lai) have received a benefit in the purchase....you appear to have obtained a pecuniary benefit," Jeyaretnam said.
But Lai dismissed the petition, saying discount purchases were above board -- as parliament had agreed.

Lai also ordered Jeyaretnam, whom he accused of not verifying his client's "inaccurate" submissions, to pay costs and referred the Worker's Party leader to the Law Society, the ruling body for lawyers, for disciplinary action.
